claims.text: Source-2 gives only the distinct \((i,k,\mu)\)-bordered Jacobi–Trudi lemma and its matrix construction. [source-2@L1697-L1742|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1697: \begin{lemma}
1698: \label{Woo-2nd-lemma}
1699: Let $i < k$, and assume $\mu$ is a partition with
1700: $
1701: \mu_k > i \geq \mu_{k+1},
1702: $
1703: so that the $(i+1)^{st}$ column of the Young diagram for $\mu$ has length $k > i$.
1704: Then
1705: $$
1706: s_\mu = \sum_{m=1}^k (-1)^{k-m} \,\, h_{\mu_m+k-i-m} \,\, s_{\mu^{(m)}},
1707: $$
1708: where for $m=1,2,\ldots,k$ one defines
1709: $$
1710: \mu^{(m)}:=(\mu_1,\mu_2,\ldots,\mu_{m-1},\widehat{\mu_m}, \mu_{m+1}-1,\mu_{m+2}-1,
1711:                \ldots,\mu_k-1,i,\mu_{k+1},\mu_{k+2},\ldots,\mu_{\ell}),
1712: $$
1713: where $\ell:=\ell(\mu)$ and $\widehat{\mu_m}$ refers to the deletion of
1714: the entry $\mu_m$.
1715: %
1716: %In particular, for each $m=1,2,\ldots,k$ in the sum, the
1717: %factor $h_{\mu_m+k-i-m}$ has positive degree (since $\mu_m \geq i+1$), 
1718: %and each $\lambda^{(m)}$ also has $\lambda^{(m)}_j \geq i$.
1719: \end{lemma}
1720: \begin{proof}
1721: Start with the $\ell \times \ell$
1722: Jacobi-Trudi matrix for $\mu$.  From this create an $(\ell+1) \times \ell$ matrix by inserting a 
1723: new row between its row $k$ and row $k+1$, having entries 
1724: $$
1725: (h_{i-k+1},h_{i-k+2},\ldots,h_{i-k+\ell}).
1726: $$  
1727: Then from this $(\ell+1) \times \ell$ matrix, create a singular $(\ell+1) \times (\ell+1)$ matrix 
1728: by introducing an $(\ell+1)^{st}$ column that
1729: duplicates the $(k-i)^{th}$ column.  This last duplicated column is
1730: $$
1731: \begin{array}{lccrll}
1732: \ \ \ \ (h_{\mu_1+k-i-1},\ldots,h_{\mu_k-i},
1733:    &h_{i-k + (k-i)},&h_{\mu_{k+1}-i-1},&\ldots, &h_{\mu_{\ell}+k-i-\ell}&)^T \\
1734: = (h_{\mu_1+k-i-1},\ldots,h_{\mu_k-i},
1735:    &1,            &0,              &\ldots,&0&)^T.
1736: \end{array}
1737: $$
1738: Here we have used the facts that $h_0=1$ and that $h_{\mu_m+k-i-m}=0$ 
1739: for $m \geq k+1$ because $\mu_m \leq \mu_{k+1} \leq i$ implies 
1740: $\mu_m+k-i-m=(\mu_m-i)+(k-m)<0$.
1741: One then checks that cofactor expanding the (zero) determinant of this 
1742: $(\ell+1) \times (\ell+1)$ matrix along this duplicated column gives the asserted identity.
